newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian cosmonauts leave Mir, enter Soyuz capsule.
newsitem.headline: Russian cosmonauts leave Mir, enter Soyuz capsule.

text.p: Two Russian cosmonauts, due to return to Earth after perhaps the toughest assignment in the history of manned space flights, left the Mir space station on Thursday and entered a Soyuz spacecraft.

"I hope that everything bad that we've had will leave with us," said outgoing Mir commander Vasily Tsibliyev. "We are leaving. See you on Earth," he told the remaining crew. The hatches between Mir and Soyuz are due to be locked at 0550 GMT.
Tsibliyev's remarks were carried on a television screen at Mission Control.
A Mission official said later the returning crew members sealed the hatches of the airlock between Mir and Soyuz at 9.47 a.m. (0547 GMT) and started checking how airtight they were.
Tsibliyev and flight engineeer Alexander Lazutkin are scheduled to set off at 12.53 p.m. (0853 GMT) and land at 4.16 p.m. (1216 GMT) in the former Soviet republic of Kazakhstan.

They and NASA astronaut Michael Foale, who will stay aboard Mir till September, have endured a series of major woes since they boarded the space station in February. The most serious incident was a June 25 collision between Mir and a resupply craft.
